fig1_model_vs_baseline.title: Model vs. baseline precision
fig1_model_vs_baseline.caption: Frozen Week-4 hand-written rule vs. Logistic Regression vs. Random Forest on 5 client-held-out GroupShuffleSplit folds. Bars show mean precision@K; error bars show ± 1 std. The Random Forest's precision@200 of 75.6% is 22.7 percentage points above the Week-4 rule (52.9%) and 15.9 pp above chance (59.7%).

fig2_split_inflation.title: Random vs. grouped split
fig2_split_inflation.caption: The same Random Forest evaluated under two split designs. Random ShuffleSplit produces inflated prec@200 of 89.8% by leaking client-memorized patterns into test. GroupShuffleSplit by client_id (the honest design) reports 75.6% — a 14.2 pp gap we explicitly conservatively choose.

fig3_staleness_signal.title: Staleness vs. severe-decline rate
fig3_staleness_signal.caption: Staleness buckets confirm the flag assumption behind the Week-4 rule. Severe-decline rate rises monotonically from 58.3% (<90d) to 74.3% (≥180d), and median trend_pct drops from −30.8% to −44.5%.

fig4_playbook_archetypes.title: Playbook archetype × action crosstab
fig4_playbook_archetypes.caption: 5 archetype buckets (rows) mapped to REFRESH / OBSERVE / IGNORE actions from the Week-7 ranked playbook. VERY_STALE_HIGH_VIS (n=12) and STRIKING_DISTANCE (n=282) concentrate REFRESH candidates; 90.9% of items are IGNORE.
